doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Algiers places, ball games and Frankie Duson
title: Tom plays for the soldiers, buys music on Charter Street, and key trombones
summary: Tom recalls playing for soldiers when the Naval Station building opened, and buying his cornet books at a store on Charter Street. He says trombonists then played key trombones, not slides, including Buddy Johnson and Frankie Duson.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: That's all? Yeah. Of course, I used to play for the soldiers. When they first built a building there, at the Naval Station, when the... The dock, the dock come in about six o'clock that morning, they had built a kind of thing on the levee, you know, but they had built that big building over there. I believe that was what, number 11? Number 11. So they had soldiers there then. And so Lowe, they just had come here. That's the first time I Lowe I see them.
Yeah, I think I was playing violin, and I'd take them to play a cornet with me that time.

First time I knew it, he must have just had come here, but the fellow, George, he said he'd get me a cornet play, so he got a little, and I had those red books. No, I used to get books right at the corner where you had your shop, you know where you had your shop? Yeah, Charter Street. Oh, Charter Street, that old man there. Used to be in Two Bitsville.
Yeah, I heard there was a music store.

Oh yeah, I used to get all my music there. Yeah, that old man, I don't forgot it. Yeah, I don't remember that. Yeah, but it was on this side, that's why I used to get all the music, right from that old man there on Charter Street. That's on there where that gunsmith was.

Yeah. I used to get all our music there. But music used to be cheap then, you used to get them, you know, get books. Used to have them little books, the cornet. But they didn't have no saxophone and drums. They didn't have that then. Yeah. And they used to use these key tramoses. They wasn't using the slides. And now, that's the first time I've seen slides. His brother started to slide in allergies with slides. They tell me Buddy, that's what he was blowing. Who was that?
Buddy Johnson. He was playing key. Key.
And Frankie Deuce was playing key tramoses. All of us used to play key tramoses.
Yeah, Carnish, I know they say Carnish.
Yeah, Joe Petit. Yeah, Joe Petit. All of us used to play key tramoses. Because afterwards, they didn't always get in the slides.
